title: Valuing American Options by Simulation: A Simple Least-Squares Approach
verification: Transcribed from extracted PDF text and visually checked against a rendering of journal page 127.
printed_precision: All reported prices and standard errors are rounded to 0.001 in the original table.

protocol.stock_process: Risk-neutral geometric Brownian motion with constant rate and volatility, zero dividends.
protocol.regressors: Constant, exp(-x/2), exp(-x/2)*(1-x), exp(-x/2)*(1-2*x+x*x/2), with x=S/K.
protocol.regression_sample: Only in-the-money paths at each exercise date.
protocol.regression_target: Future realized cashflow, discounted to the regression date; stock and cashflows normalized by strike for fitting.
protocol.valuation: In-sample stopping-rule fit and valuation; discount actual realized stopped cashflows to time zero and average.
protocol.early_exercise_value: Simulated American value minus the closed-form Black-Scholes European value; no European control variate is stated for Table 1.
protocol.finite_difference_reference: Published implicit finite difference results, 40000 time steps per year and 1000 stock-price steps, compared with explicit finite difference results.
unreported_details: The paper does not publish its random-number generator, seeds, or normal-generation algorithm.
The paper does not state the standard-error calculation formula; its antithetic convention cannot be claimed exactly from the text.
The finite difference stock-domain bounds and complete numerical boundary implementation are not specified in Section 3.
A separately computed CRR tree is an additional numerical reference, not a reproduction of the paper's finite difference implementation.
